newsitem.title: GAMBIA: Electoral officer calls for peaceful poll in Gambia.
newsitem.headline: Electoral officer calls for peaceful poll in Gambia.

text.p: Gambia's electoral officer called on Wednesday for a peaceful presidential poll on Thursday following a violent election campaign in the army-ruled West African country.

Gabriel Roberts, chairman of the Provisional Independent Electoral Commission, urged voters to create no disturbances. The commission "expects an atmosphere of real calm to return to the Gambia", he said.
Colonel Yahya Jammeh, who led a coup in 1994, is one of four hopefuls seeking election as president in the small West African country at the end of two years of army rule.
During a bruising election campaign Jammeh's car was stoned and his supporters clashed with those of his main rival, lawyer Ousainou Darboe. The capital was calm on Wednesday.
Polling starts at 7 a.m. (0700 GMT) and ends at 6 p.m. (1800 GMT). First results are expected late on Thursday.
Gambia is a mainly Moslem former British colony of just over one million people.
Jammeh excluded the country's established politicians from the poll when he banned anyone who served as a minister under ousted president Sir Dawda Jawara from standing.
Jammeh and other junior officers toppled Jawara accusing him of corruption.
